notes.baseline_conflict: PulseWear is the load-state spec; every formula in docs/12-16 was calibrated against Nadi Wear. Running them against this seed will not reproduce any documented result. Tracked as P0 in docs/10-implementation-gaps.md.
notes.fixed_costs_inr: Source states a monthly figure (Rs 26 L). Seeded as the quarterly equivalent, Rs 78,00,000, matching docs/README.md's comparison table.
notes.opening_customers: Active Customers (530). Source also gives 920 Registered Customers; which one the referral cap multiplies is not stated.
notes.employee_satisfaction: Left null. Source gives Employee Morale 76 and Employee Productivity 81, neither named Employee Satisfaction. Mapping morale onto the satisfaction curve would be an assumption.
notes.brand_score: Left null. Source gives Brand Awareness 8/100, Brand Trust 55, Brand Reputation 58. Brand Score in the Q1 model is a small accumulating quantity (0 to 8.7 over one quarter), not a 0-100 rating, so no mapping is safe.
notes.quality_score: Left null. Source gives Product Quality 72/100, which is a 0-100 rating; the Q1 model's Quality Score accumulates from zero (9.95 after one quarter). Different scales.
notes.unstated_constants: manufacturing_cost_floor, working_capital_buffer, holding cost, warranty claim cost, referral cost/cap, cost per hire, core team size and the Compliance/Forecast/Audit/Engagement baselines are all absent from docs/03. The Nadi Wear values must not be borrowed -- they are that company's economics.
notes.not_modelled: Source §11 gives hidden engine state (Strategic Thinking 50, Investor Confidence 60, Employee Burnout 10, etc.). That is cognitive-layer state, not spend-line input, so it is out of scope for this config.
